name: Bank FX purchase + outward wire — overseas individual with documented current-account RMB income
who: 境外个人 (a US citizen classified on passport)
governing_instrument: 汇发〔2020〕14号 Art. 59 (purchase) + Art. 65(1) (remittance); PBOC Order [2006] No. 3 Art. 13
documents_required: Valid ID + amount-bearing source-of-funds documents for the purchase, INCLUDING a tax certificate
amount_ceiling_stated_in_text: No ceiling stated in Art. 59 or Art. 65(1)
pros: The only route in the reviewed instruments that both converts and remits on documents rather than on a quota; no annual cap appears in the text; a single wire is permitted because Art. 65(1) states no amount threshold; the tax certificate you need is evidence of tax already paid, not a new conversion tax
cons: The bank decides whether your documents are sufficient and may refuse under Art. 68; the tax certificate must exist, so unpaid PRC tax on the underlying income blocks the route; branch practice varies because much of the guidance is branch-level Q&A

name: Bank FX purchase + outward wire — domestic individual above the convenience amount, on purpose documents
who: 境内个人 (a Chinese citizen, or a foreigner continuously resident 1 year on the Order 532 reading)
documents_required: Valid ID + amount-bearing documents on the PURPOSE of the purchase funds + a completed 个人购汇申请书; above USD 50,000/day on the remittance leg, amount-bearing materials
amount_ceiling_stated_in_text: USD 50,000 per person per year is a DOCUMENTATION threshold, not a cap (SAFE Ningxia 2022)
pros: Works for any amount provided the documents exist; the purchase above the convenience amount expressly does not occupy the quota; e-banking and counter are both permitted under Art. 55
cons: Art. 57 makes you personally and legally responsible for the accuracy of the 购汇申请书; Art. 64(1) requires the purchase purpose and the remittance purpose to be consistent, and the bank reviews that; Art. 62 makes splitting a watch-list offence

name: Remit foreign currency you ALREADY hold in an FX account — no purchase, no spread
who: 境外个人: Art. 65(1), ID only. 境内个人: Art. 64(1), ID up to USD 50,000/day, ID + documents above
documents_required: Valid ID (overseas individual). Domestic individual above USD 50,000/day also needs amount-bearing materials
amount_ceiling_stated_in_text: Art. 65(1) states NO amount threshold for an overseas individual
pros: Cheapest route that exists: with no purchase there is no bid/ask spread at all, so the only published cost is the wire fee and the telecom charge; an overseas individual needs nothing but ID
cons: Only available if the balance is already in foreign currency; a CNY balance cannot use it; the remittance must still be current-account in character

name: Annual convenience amount — FX purchase on identity document alone
who: 境内个人 for purchase; 境外个人 ONLY if holding a Foreign Permanent Residence Identity Card. All individuals for SETTLEMENT (USD->CNY)
governing_instrument: 汇发〔2020〕14号 Arts. 54, 55, 59 para 2; PBOC Order [2006] No. 3 Arts. 9, 40
documents_required: Valid ID only, inside the amount
amount_ceiling_stated_in_text: USD 50,000 equivalent per person per year, expressly NOT a limit on the total you may transact
pros: The simplest paperwork of any route: counter or e-banking on ID alone; SAFE Ningxia states in terms that it is not an annual ceiling
cons: A US citizen without a Chinese permanent-residence ID does not get it for PURCHASE under Art. 59 para 2 — this is the single most commonly mis-stated point in the repository's earlier layers; above the amount you are back to producing documents anyway

name: Emigrant property transfer (移民财产转移)
who: A person emigrating who is cancelling a Chinese household registration
documents_required: Application to the SAFE branch at the ORIGINAL hukou location; property-right documents (notarisation abolished in 2014); the household-registration cancellation certificate
amount_ceiling_stated_in_text: No amount ceiling stated; the RMB 500,000 head-office filing requirement was abolished in 2014
pros: Since 2014 a SINGLE lump-sum remittance is permitted — the earlier installment requirement was abolished; the head-office filing above RMB 500,000 was abolished; notarisation of property documents and of agency agreements was abolished
cons: Unavailable to a US citizen who never held a Chinese hukou; gated by the IIT Law Art. 13 para 4 tax clearance, which must be completed BEFORE the hukou is cancelled; approval is discretionary and evidence-heavy

name: Inheritance property transfer (继承财产转移)
who: An heir of a decedent who held a Chinese household registration
documents_required: Application to the SAFE branch at the decedent's PRE-DEATH hukou location; since 2014 inheritances from different decedents may be combined in one application
pros: Combined applications permitted since 2014; one lump sum or installments at the applicant's choice within the approved amount
cons: Requires a Chinese decedent with a hukou; approval is discretionary; the underlying estate must be documented

name: Proceeds of selling onshore real property you own
who: 境外个人 who owns onshore commercial residential property
governing_instrument: PBOC Order [2006] No. 3 Art. 22; IIT Law Arts. 3(3), 6(5), 15 para 2
documents_required: SAFE approval for the purchase-and-remit; the IIT payment certificate is inspected before the property transfer is registered
pros: A genuine capital-account exit for property wealth; the 20% IIT is charged on the GAIN (proceeds less original value and reasonable expenses), not on the sale price, and is creditable in principle against U.S. tax
cons: You must actually own and sell the property; SAFE approval is required before the FX purchase; the 20% IIT on the gain is a real cash cost that must be paid before the money can move

name: Investor's share of a lawfully liquidated foreign-invested enterprise
who: The foreign investor in a terminated FIE
documents_required: Evidence of lawful termination, completed liquidation and tax payment
pros: Expressly provided for in a State Council administrative regulation — the highest-ranking instrument reviewed; covers capital, not just income
cons: Only available where there is a real enterprise, a real liquidation and tax actually paid; the liquidation itself takes time and professional cost; Art. 22 para 3 speaks to the RMB 'belonging to the foreign investor', so personal savings are out of scope

name: Company profit / dividend remittance
legal_status: Lawful if the money belongs to the company
who: A domestic institution distributing profit to a foreign shareholder
documents_required: Board (or partnership) profit-distribution resolution + the ORIGINAL tax filing form for remittances above USD 50,000; the bank stamps the original with the amount and date
amount_ceiling_stated_in_text: USD 50,000 is a document-review threshold, not a cap; the old limit tied to 'dividends payable + undistributed profits' in the latest audit report was abolished in 2014
pros: The 2014 reform removed the audit-report and capital-verification-report review above USD 50,000 and abolished the undistributed-profits ceiling; a real corporate route for real corporate money
cons: Not a personal route at all — using it for personal savings is a disguised transfer and engages Order 532 Art. 39; corporate income tax and withholding tax fall before the remittance; the tax recordal must exist

name: Service-trade outward payment against a genuine service contract
legal_status: Lawful if the transaction is genuine
who: A domestic institution or individual paying for a real cross-border service
documents_required: Contract, invoice or settlement list showing the subject matter, parties and amount; above USD 50,000 per transaction, tax recordal first and the bank verifies the recordal form
amount_ceiling_stated_in_text: USD 50,000 per transaction is a review/recordal threshold, not a cap
pros: A legitimate channel for genuine services; below USD 50,000 the bank in principle need not review the documents at all
cons: Art. 47 expressly forbids fabricating a trade background and forbids evading FX control by splitting; a payment without a real service behind it is 非法套汇 under Order 532 Art. 40 with a fine up to 30% (30%-100% where serious)

name: Convert back RMB left over from an earlier exchange
who: 境外个人 who previously exchanged FX into RMB and did not use it all
documents_required: Valid ID + the ORIGINAL EXCHANGE SLIP; slip valid for conversion back for 24 months from the exchange date
amount_ceiling_stated_in_text: Up to USD 500 equivalent same-day on ID alone; up to USD 1,000 equivalent same-day at pre-departure locations outside the customs area
pros: No source-of-funds documentation beyond the slip; the small same-day amounts need nothing but ID
cons: Only reverses an exchange you already made — it cannot export money that originated as RMB; hard 24-month expiry on the slip

name: Return unused FX that was remitted IN, along the original route
who: 境外个人 with FX previously remitted into China and not used
documents_required: Valid ID
pros: Identity document only; the simplest reversal route in the reviewed instruments
cons: Only for money that came IN from abroad and was not used; it is a refund path, not an export path for domestically earned CNY

name: Entrust a close relative to act for you
who: Any individual; 近亲属 means spouse, parents, children, siblings, paternal and maternal grandparents, paternal and maternal grandchildren
documents_required: Both parties' valid IDs + a power of attorney + relationship documentation (hukou book, marriage certificate, birth certificate; a commitment letter may substitute where these genuinely cannot be provided)
amount_ceiling_stated_in_text: Within the convenience amount for quota-occupying business; with amount-bearing materials for non-quota-occupying business
pros: A genuine convenience where you are not in China; the relationship can be evidenced by a commitment letter where documents cannot be obtained
cons: This is agency for YOUR OWN genuine transaction. Using a relative's quota to move your money is exactly the borrowing that Art. 62(2) puts on the watch list for three years, and it exposes the relative under Art. 62(1)

name: Carry foreign cash across the border
who: Any individual
governing_instrument: 汇发〔2020〕14号 Arts. 86, 89; State Council Order 532 Art. 42; PBOC Order [2006] No. 3 Arts. 33-35
documents_required: Inbound above USD 5,000 equivalent: written declaration to Customs. Outbound USD 5,000-10,000 with no or exceeded inbound record: a Permit for Carrying FX Out of the Country from a BANK. Outbound above USD 10,000 to a war-affected, strictly-controlled or financially unstable country: the permit from the SAFE BRANCH
amount_ceiling_stated_in_text: Withdrawal from a bank: up to USD 10,000 equivalent cumulative per day on ID; above that, SAFE branch pre-filing and a 提取外币现钞备案表 valid 30 days and not reusable
pros: No wire fee and no spread if the cash already exists
cons: Physically impractical at the amounts in this brief; Order 532 Art. 42 allows a fine of up to 20% of the amount for carrying FX across the border in violation of the rules; on arrival in the United States a currency amount above USD 10,000 must be reported and failure to report is separately penalised under 31 U.S.C. §5321(a)(2)

name: Remit CNY and convert abroad (cross-border RMB)
legal_status: Lawful if the underlying transaction is genuine
who: A payer with a genuine current-account or approved capital-account obligation denominated in RMB
governing_instrument: State Council Order 532 Art. 5; 汇发〔2020〕14号 Art. 54
documents_required: The same authenticity documentation as the underlying transaction; the receiving bank and any offshore RMB liquidity determine execution
pros: Moves the conversion offshore, so the onshore bid/ask spread is not paid; Art. 5 confirms current-account payments and transfers are not restricted
cons: Requires a counterparty willing to receive CNY and a genuine transaction; the offshore CNY/CNH rate and the receiving bank's charges are NOT published by any official source reviewed here, so the cost is left BLANK and flagged; does not work for exporting your own savings with no counterparty

name: Domestic transfer between your own accounts, or to a close relative
who: Any individual
governing_instrument: 汇发〔2020〕14号 Art. 67; PBOC Order [2006] No. 3 Arts. 28, 32
documents_required: Valid ID; the accounts must belong to the same subject category
amount_ceiling_stated_in_text: Transfers are limited to between the person's own accounts and between the person and close relatives, of the SAME subject category
pros: Useful for consolidating balances before a single outward wire, which minimises the fixed telecom charge
cons: Does not move money out of China at all; a transfer between a domestic-individual account and an overseas-individual account is managed as a CROSS-BORDER transaction and must satisfy the outward-remittance rules; FX savings accounts cannot be used for business receipts and payments

name: Quota splitting across several people (分拆)
who: n/a
governing_instrument: 汇发〔2020〕14号 Art. 62; PBOC Order [2006] No. 3 Art. 7; State Council Order 532 Arts. 39, 40; 31 U.S.C. §5321(a)(4)
documents_required: n/a
cons: Expressly forbidden. Art. 62 puts both the borrower and the lender of a quota on a watch list for the year of listing plus two further years. Order 532 Art. 39 and Art. 40 both carry a fine of up to 30% of the amount, rising to 30%-100% where the circumstances are serious. On the U.S. side, 31 U.S.C. §5321(a)(4) permits a structuring penalty of up to the FULL AMOUNT of the currency involved.

name: Underground bank / informal value transfer (地下钱庄)
who: n/a
governing_instrument: State Council Order 532 Art. 45; PBOC Order [2006] No. 3 Art. 39
documents_required: n/a
cons: Order 532 Art. 45: warning, confiscation of illegal gains and a fine of up to 30% of the illegal amount for privately buying or selling FX, doing so in disguised form, scalping, or illegally brokering in a relatively large amount; 30%-100% where the circumstances are serious; criminal liability where a crime is constituted. In the United States the same flow is a money-laundering exposure and forfeitable.

name: Buy cryptocurrency with CNY, sell abroad for USD
who: n/a
documents_required: n/a
cons: The exchange of CNY for a token offshore and back into USD is 变相买卖外汇 (buying or selling FX in disguised form) within Art. 45 where it is used to move value across the border, and Art. 39 reaches the unlawful outward transfer of onshore capital by deceptive means: up to 30%, and 30%-100% where serious, plus criminal exposure. No official instrument reviewed here authorises the route.

name: False invoices or false transaction documents
who: n/a
governing_instrument: State Council Order 532 Art. 40; 汇发〔2020〕14号 Arts. 47, 62, 68; PBOC Order [2006] No. 3 Art. 7
documents_required: n/a
cons: Art. 40 treats fraudulently purchasing FX with false or invalid transaction documents as 非法套汇: the funds are ordered converted back and a fine of up to 30% is imposed, 30%-100% where serious, with criminal liability where a crime is constituted. Art. 7 forbids using false commercial documents to evade authenticity management and Art. 68 entitles the bank to refuse.
